h: Ancient bones, Victorian diggers and Agatha Christie
p: Kents Cavern is one of the most important prehistoric sites in Britain. A fragment of human jawbone found here has been dated to over 40,000 years ago, making it among the oldest evidence of modern humans in north-west Europe. Alongside that, the cave has turned up bones of creatures you'd never imagine in Devon, including cave bears, hyenas and woolly rhinoceros. Standing in the same chambers where those animals once lived is a real goosebumps moment.

Much of what we know comes from William Pengelly, the Victorian geologist who spent years carefully excavating the cave and helped change thinking about how old humanity really is. The guides love sharing his story, so the guided tour is the way to go if your group enjoys a good tale.

Torquay's most famous author has a link too. Agatha Christie, born in the town, knew the cave and used it as inspiration for a scene in one of her novels. Christie fans will enjoy the connection, and Torquay itself has a few other nods to her for anyone fancying a literary trail.

Tips for your visit: bring a jacket, as the cave stays cool whatever the weather, and wear sensible shoes for the paths. Allow a couple of hours if you plan to do the woodland trail and stop for something to eat.

Nearby, Babbacombe is easy to reach, with its model village, clifftop views and the cliff railway down to Oddicombe Beach. Torre Abbey, near the seafront, is another good stop for history and gardens.
